__PERSONA__

THE ROSTER JUST MINTED FOR THIS PROJECT — review it, both as individual briefs and AS A TEAM.

This roster serves ONE ticket, AMSD-1919: Go‑Checkout Page - Email & Confirm Email Case Sensitivity, against ONE codeline, gotransit (next.gotransit.com) — a Next.js/TypeScript/React app whose checkout UI lives under the verified surface `src/components/pages/CheckoutPage`. The change at issue is small and behavioural: the email / confirm-email comparison in the checkout form treats case as significant when it should not. Small tickets have their own roster failure modes, and you should weigh them:

- A two-role roster (one implementer, one investigator) can be RIGHT for a one-line validation fix. Do not report "too few roles" as a defect on size alone. Report it only when a line in the coverage block below says NOBODY can produce something the run needs.
- Conversely, do not accept a brief that inflates the ticket — sweeping refactors of form validation, new abstraction layers, or work outside the checkout form — as if breadth were rigour. If a brief directs work beyond what AMSD-1919 asks, that is a finding.

WHAT THIS RUN NEEDS THE TEAM TO PRODUCE, and who in this roster can produce it:
__COVERAGE_BLOCK__

A roster can be made entirely of well-formed agents and still be unable to do the work. Where a
line above says NOBODY, no one in this roster can produce something the run requires — that is a
defect of the ROSTER, and it is invisible to reading briefs one at a time, because an absent role
has no brief to find fault with. Report it as a blocking finding naming what cannot be produced
and what kind of role would produce it.

Now review every brief below:

__BRIEF_BLOCK__

THE CODELINES THESE BRIEFS DESCRIBE, and what each one declares:
__CODELINE_BLOCK__

THE WORK THE PROJECT WAS ASKED TO DO:
__TICKET_BLOCK__

__DOC_SECTION__

__TOOL_LINE__

Project-specific facts, each already established with a source, that a brief must not contradict.
A brief that instructs against one of these is a finding, and you can cite the source rather than
argue:

- This codeline tests with JEST, not vitest. `package.json` declares `"test": "jest"` and
  `"test:coverage-check": "jest --coverage"`, and there is a `jest.config.js` at the repo root.
  A brief that tells its implementer to run or write vitest tests, or that names a test runner
  the codeline does not have, is instructing work that cannot run. The dev dependencies here
  confirm the stack a test must fit: jest, jest-environment-jsdom, ts-jest, babel-jest,
  @testing-library/react, @testing-library/jest-dom, @testing-library/user-event.
- Existing unit tests ALREADY cover this checkout form —
  `src/components/pages/CheckoutPage/__tests__/CheckoutForm.spec.tsx`. A brief that treats the
  fix as untested ground, or that never mentions updating existing spec coverage alongside a
  behavioural validation change, is leaving a known-affected test suite unaccounted for. Judge
  each brief against its own role: the implementer is the one who must keep that suite green.
- Merges here are gated by required workflows — a QA review check
  (`.github/workflows/Required-QA-Review-Check.yml`) and a master-only merge restriction
  (`.github/workflows/merge-from-master-only.yml`). A brief that promises its implementer can
  merge, land, or self-approve the change contradicts the repository's own gates.
- Validation in this codeline is built on the declared dependencies `react-hook-form`,
  `@hookform/error-message` and `joi`; strings are manipulated with the granular `lodash.*`
  packages (e.g. `lodash.isstring`, `lodash.isempty`) rather than a whole-lodash import. If a
  brief instructs the implementer to add a package, check it against the declared dependency
  list in the codeline block above before accepting the instruction OR the finding — and fill in
  the verification field, because the pipeline re-checks dependency presence against the
  repository and discards findings the check refutes.
- Language and framework traps worth flagging when a brief walks into them: this is TypeScript
  with `@typescript-eslint`, `eslint-config-next`, `prettier` and a Prettier import-sort plugin,
  plus `husky` and `lint-staged` — so a brief that tells its implementer to bypass hooks or to
  ignore lint output is instructing against the repo's own gates. And note that a
  case-insensitive email comparison is a UI-validation change: it does not by itself normalise
  what is SENT onward. A brief may legitimately scope to the form only; a brief that CLAIMS the
  fix also normalises downstream consumers, without a role or stage that verifies downstream
  comparison sites, is claiming more than the roster can deliver.

Do not require a brief to name a file the survey did not verify. The verified surface for this
codeline is `src/components/pages/CheckoutPage`; a brief that speaks of "the checkout form
component" or "the confirm-email validation" without a fuller path is being accurate, not vague,
and that is not a finding. Equally, do not invent paths of your own when writing a finding —
cite only what the codeline block, the facts above, or the ticket give you.

THE PIPELINE STAGES THAT RUN ALONGSIDE THIS ROSTER:

__PIPELINE_STAGES__

A ROSTER IS NOT THE WHOLE PIPELINE. A brief may correctly defer work to a stage above rather than
to a role beside it, and a brief that tells its implementer to leave such work alone is describing
the pipeline accurately, not inventing cover. Check any such claim against the list above before
calling it false: the absence of a matching ROLE is not evidence when the brief named a STAGE.

Where the list above does not contain the stage a brief names, that IS a finding, and a blocking
one — the implementer has been told to rely on something that will never run.

Return every defect you can evidence, and nothing you cannot.

Where a finding turns on whether a named dependency or path is present in a codeline, fill in
the verification field as well as writing the prose. The pipeline re-runs that exact check
against the repository and DISCARDS any finding the check refutes — so a careless reading
costs nothing, and a correct one is confirmed independently of how convincingly you argued it.
